1.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/lib/stack-collector.js is where Lighthouse pulls in both the original js-library-detector results and the new Fast-Path detector results without merging or deduplicating by id.  
• lighthouse-core/lib/stack-packs.js maps the raw detection results to the static stack-pack metadata and shovels every entry into the LHR, again with no filtering or dedupe logic.  
• lighthouse-core/audits/dobetterweb/js-libraries.js is the audit that surfaces library detections to the user; it currently shows both stable and experimental entries so the “React (Fast Path)” pack appears alongside the normal “React” pack in the Best Practices → JavaScript Libraries view.  
• stack-packs/index.js and stack-packs/packs/react.js define the canonical React pack (title, icon, help text) but have no notion of excluding experimental detections or merging duplicates by id, so adding or normalizing an explicit id here would be part of a proper fix.
1.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse (or PageSpeed Insights) against https://abcnews.go.com/ and look at the “Minify JavaScript” audit under the Best Practices category, you’ll see two identical React stack-pack entries – same icon, title and help text – rendered one after another. In the raw JSON there are two items in lhr.stackPacks both with id “react”: one from the original js-library-detector, and one from the new “Fast Path” experimental checks. The code never deduplicates these, and there’s no filtering of experimental packs, so both end up in the report.

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/lib/stack-collector.js is where Lighthouse pulls in stack packs from both the static pack definitions and the js-library-detector (including the new Fast Path checks). Because it matches and merges packs by title instead of a unique id, it ends up pushing two React entries into lhr.stackPacks.
• lighthouse-core/lib/stack-packs.js contains the core logic for loading, normalizing, and formatting stack packs before they’re delivered to the report. It currently has no deduplication keyed on an explicit id, so duplicates slip through.
• stack-packs/index.js is the entry point that registers all of the built-in packs (amp, angular, magento, react, wordpress). It wires in the static React pack definition that our duplicate is colliding with.
• stack-packs/packs/react.js is the static pack definition for React (title, icon, help text). The new Fast Path detector also reports React, so you get two identical definitions in the final output.
• lighthouse-core/audits/dobetterweb/js-libraries.js is the Best Practices audit that surfaces the stack-pack entries to the user. It doesn’t filter out duplicates, so any doubling in lhr.stackPacks appears directly in the rendered audit UI.
2.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse (or PageSpeed Insights) against https://abcnews.go.com/ and view the “Minify JavaScript” audit under the “Best Practices” category, you see two identical React stack-pack entries rendered back-to-back (same icon, title, and help text). If you dump the JSON (`lhr.stackPacks`), there are two elements both with id “react” – one coming from the original js-library-detector integration and the other from the new “Fast Path” checks added in the Library-Detector pull request.
